title_formula_note: Chosen: T11 'Could [Animal] Survive Every [Set]?' per brief section 1 and decisions.md (single '?' approved for this T11 episode, as with 023). The working title's 'Deadly' is not in the dread set (rule 4), so the lead swaps it for the death verb 'Died' at the end: 'Before and After It Died' keeps the brief's before/after promise and states outright that megalodon is dead, which closes the HIGH 'still alive' packaging risk in the title itself. Rule check: (1) 59 chars, 10 words; (2) Title Case, no caps, emoji or '!', one '?' (CD exception); (3) T11; (4) one death verb 'Died', no dread adjective; (5) scope 'Every'; (6) no 'in N Minutes', no count at all (no '10' or '11': the video has 11 stops); (7) see thumbnail_brief word list; (9) 5 candidates; (10) not a Paint Explainer title or noun swap, and none of Fossil's wording ('Dominate', 'Prehistoric Ocean'). Bans respected in all five: no 'still alive', 'hiding', 'The Meg', 'Weirdest', 'dino'. Not 023's kicker 'Doug Died Trying'/'Checking'. Alternates: T11 with a Doug kicker (closest A/B to the lead; Doug dies 8 times); a T4-style revelation 'Only One Actually Killed It' (honest: only the boss verdict is on record, the rest are hedged guesses); a 'Which Era' question with scope 'Every One'; and a T11 'Most of Them Kill It' (7 of 11 stops are losses). The CD's favourite 'Every Era That Would Kill Megalodon, and the One That Did' was not used because megalodon survives 4 of the 11 stops, so 'Every Era That Would Kill' over-promises.

description:
Megalodon has been extinct for about 3.6 million years, so what would happen if you dropped one into the deadliest eras before and after its own? Doug rides along in a shark cage, from a Panama shark nursery and the age of mosasaurs to a nearby supernova, the Ice Age, the Panama Canal and the deep-sea floor where old shark teeth turn up.

Where should Doug take a megalodon next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe so you're here for Doug's next bad idea.
